episodes.title: Pilot
probes: A documentary crew turns up at the Scranton paper company for the first time, filming the staff at their desks.
A young temporary worker starts his first day at the branch and is shown around the office.

episodes.title: Diversity Day
probes: Michael tapes index cards with different races written on them to everyone's foreheads and makes them act out stereotypes.
An outside consultant arrives to run a tolerance session, and Michael keeps interrupting to deliver his own version.
The whole office is herded into the conference room for a mandatory seminar about race and tolerance.

episodes.title: Health Care
probes: Jim and Pam entertain themselves filling out the medical forms Dwight has handed around the office.
Dwight is put in charge of picking the office's new health care plan, and takes the job very seriously.
Michael promises the whole office a big surprise, then spends the day scrambling to come up with one.

episodes.title: The Alliance
probes: Michael spends the whole day agonizing over what joke to write in a coworker's birthday card.
The office holds a morale-boosting birthday party for an employee whose birthday is over a month away.
With downsizing rumors swirling, paranoia spreads through the office and Dwight starts talking in Survivor terms.

episodes.title: Basketball
probes: The office staff square off against the warehouse crew in a basketball game, losers owing a Saturday shift.
Michael assembles his lineup by looks and assumptions, passing over the more athletic office workers for weaker players.
Michael stops play mid-game to insist on a "flagrant personal intentional foul" against his side.

episodes.title: Hot Girl
probes: A visiting saleswoman sets up a table of purses in the office, and the men keep drifting over.
Michael and Dwight openly compete for the attention of the woman selling handbags out of the conference area.
An espresso machine turns up in the office kitchen, courtesy of Michael's spending.

episodes.title: The Dundies
probes: Michael works the microphone as emcee, handing out the yearly joke trophies his employees have learned to dread.
Pam sits through the awards ceremony getting steadily drunker as the evening goes on.
The whole branch is dragged out for the annual awards night Michael loves and everyone else loathes.

episodes.title: Sexual Harassment
probes: Michael worries that a review of the company's harassment policies will spoil what he calls his easy-going office.
The human resources representative is ordered by corporate to run a review of the branch's sexual harassment policies.
Corporate sends a lawyer down to Scranton, who spends the day sitting in on things at the branch.

episodes.title: Office Olympics
probes: Bored at their desks, Jim and Pam invent competitive games out of office supplies and rope in coworkers.
Michael sits with his realtor going over condo paperwork, unsettled by how many years the payments will run.
Michael takes Dwight along with him out of the office for the day to handle a property deal.

episodes.title: The Fire
probes: The whole staff waits outside in the parking lot after evacuating, killing time with games and questions about each other.
Michael decides to take Ryan under his wing as a mentor, and Dwight sulks about the attention.

episodes.title: Halloween
probes: It's Halloween at the branch, and Michael has spent the whole month stalling on something corporate asked of him.
The last day of October arrives with Michael dodging a decision headquarters handed him weeks earlier.

episodes.title: The Fight
probes: Michael and Dwight face off on the mats of a local dojo to settle their argument.
Michael and Dwight spend the day bickering over which of them would win in a fight.

episodes.title: The Client
probes: With the boss out of the office, the staff gather to read aloud and act out a screenplay Michael wrote.
Michael and Jan take an important client out for a long meal away from the branch.
Jan grows visibly irritated as Michael steers the client conversation anywhere but toward actual business.

episodes.title: Performance Review
probes: Michael digs through the suggestion box, treating the anonymous slips as tips for improving himself.
One by one, employees are called into Michael's office to sit through their annual performance reviews.
While reviewing everyone else, Michael keeps fretting about the review Jan is about to give him.

episodes.title: Email Surveillance
probes: Michael spends part of his evening at an improvisational comedy class, trying to distract himself.
Jim is hosting a party at his own home for people from the office.
Michael takes to reading through his employees' emails from his own desk.

episodes.title: Christmas Party
probes: At the office Christmas party, Michael turns Secret Santa into a game where everyone can steal each other's gifts.
Unhappy with what he ends up holding, Michael sets off to procure himself a better gift.
fine: The gift Michael bought for Ryan is an expensive iPod, and the whole staff keeps swapping to grab it.

episodes.title: Booze Cruise
probes: Michael rents a boat and takes the whole office out on the water for an annual motivational cruise.
Aboard the chartered boat, Michael's antics steadily get on the nerves of the man captaining it.
Roy has been drinking heavily by the time the party on the boat gets going.

episodes.title: The Injury
probes: Michael, stuck at home and unable to drive himself in, phones the office demanding someone come pick him up.

episodes.title: The Secret
probes: Oscar phones in sick, and a suspicious Dwight spends the day trying to catch him out.
Dwight appoints himself investigator of a colleague's sick day, tailing him rather than staying at his desk.

episodes.title: The Carpet
probes: Michael won't set foot in his own office after something foul is left there, and eyes his staff suspiciously.

episodes.title: Boys and Girls
probes: Jan drives down to Scranton to run a seminar just for the women of the office.
Left out of the women's seminar, Michael sulks and then throws together a session of his own for the men.
The office splits along gender lines for the day, women in one meeting and men stuck with Michael.

episodes.title: Valentine's Day
probes: All day, gift after gift arrives at one saleswoman's desk from her boyfriend, piling up for everyone to see.
Michael travels to New York City for a corporate meeting with the other branch managers.
It is Valentine's Day at the office, and Michael is away at headquarters while the staff work.

episodes.title: Dwight's Speech
probes: Dwight, jittery and pale, rehearses over and over, terrified of having to address a hall full of salesmen.
A convention hall of paper salesmen waits while Dwight, badge on, works himself into a state backstage.
Jim offers to help with Dwight's speech, quietly sourcing his suggested lines from history's most notorious orators.

episodes.title: Take Your Daughter to Work Day
probes: The office fills with employees' children for the day, kids wandering among the desks and cubicles.
Michael finds himself far happier chatting with the visiting children than with any of his adult employees.
Toby's young daughter is among the visiting kids, and Michael takes a particular shine to her.

episodes.title: Michael's Birthday
probes: Partway through the day the entire staff decamps to an ice rink and laces up skates.
Michael arrives buzzing about his own birthday while the rest of the office barely registers it.
Jim and Pam duck out of the office on a shopping run to cheer up Kevin.

episodes.title: Drug Testing
probes: Dwight finds a half-smoked joint in the parking lot and starts questioning employees one at a time.
A drug test is scheduled for the whole office, and the staff spend the day waiting to give samples.
Dwight treats his parking lot find like a criminal case, invoking his authority as a volunteer sheriff's deputy.

episodes.title: Conflict Resolution
probes: Michael stands in front of the whole staff reading aloud from files of old complaints employees made about each other.
Pam is stung that somebody complained about her doing wedding planning at work, and she wants to know who.
Toby, it turns out, has quietly kept written files on every grievance employees ever brought to him.

episodes.title: Casino Night
probes: Michael has turned the workplace into a charity casino for the evening, with gambling tables and the whole staff playing.
Michael, hosting his charity gambling evening, is fussing over being the big-shot emcee for the night.
